title: Is "AI-Slop" killing my game?
author: scaredalpaca
selftext:
Hey guys, I was just a bit bored last week and was after hanging around this sub, there's common perception that somehow AI, your game is just going to get review bombed into oblivion.

  
So I decided to check it myself. I just scraped dataset from steam curators that basically track/witchhunt AI games, basically created this analysis. filtered it down to 799 paid indie games from 2025 and 2026 to keep it relatable to this sub, pulled 95,899 reviews, and had an army of Claude Haiku instances label everything and run the numbers.

  
Quick note on what I mean by "AI slop" here: I'm counting any review that takes a derogatory shot at the game's generative AI (stuff like "AI slop", "lazy AI art", "soulless AI voices", "vibe coded garbage", and equivalents in other languages), separate from neutral or positive mentions of AI.

The short version is that there really isn't that much direct "hate" against AI games, at least from what shows up in the reviews:

* "AI slop" reviews are pretty rare. Only 0.85% of all reviews (about 1 in 118) were derogatory "AI slop" comments, and 71% of the flagged games didn't have a single one.
* Most of the malicious, low-effort stuff is negligible. Only 15% of negative "AI slop" reviews were lazy one-liners (basically the same as normal negative reviews at 14%), and only 5.6% refunded.
* Surprisingly, 60% of them actually took the time to be constructive and write out specific details about what felt broken or didn't work.
* Overall score impact is tiny unless you're a really small game with under 100 reviews (where 2 or 3 bad reviews can knock you down a tier). Disclosing AI on the store page didn't really hurt scores either.

You might feel like the whole world is against your existence right now, especially online, but there are surprisingly a lot of players out there who are willing to give you a chance.

More details obviously you can find it inside the link.  


Obviously there's a big limitation here: this doesn't account for people who "smelled" AI on the store page and decided not to buy your game in the first place. At that point though, it's impossible to measure because you're dealing with an imaginary scenario. It's kind of like piracy, where you're basically stressing over sales that you don't even know would have happened anyway.

Just a couple of personal takes after going through all this:

First, focus on your own game instead of worrying about everyone else's opinion. Putting aside the whole debate about AI stealing artists' jobs and all that, I do think there's general fatigue when it comes to looking at raw AI art. The data backs this up too: games using AI for stuff players see or hear (art, voice, music) get called "AI slop" at 2.4x the rate of games using it only for code or text. You can hide AI-generated code, you can't hide AI art. It's a huge part of your game, so the least you can do is polish it and make the experience actually feel good.

Second (and again, just a personal take), I feel like some people here don't treat this like a business. Nobody owes you attention. You have to make your product interesting enough to resonate with what players actually want, instead of expecting them to accept it as-is just because you're an indie dev who can't afford to spend money. Not trying to be callous or unsympathetic here, indie dev is tough, it's just a business at the end of the day.

Anyway, thought this might be an interesting read for you guys. Happy to answer any questions about the data!
